title.tagline: A math RPG prototype · learn once, cast many
title.journeyNote: Start in Numerola to learn the game, then travel to harder lands.

intro.p1: In the valley village of Numerola, everything runs on numbers: harvests, trade, even magic.
intro.p2: But an ancient Riddle Golem has woken in the eastern ruins and sealed the village spring. The wells are drying up.
intro.p3: You are Kai, a young ninja, and Aino, an apprentice mage. Elder Vesa is waiting for you at the west end of the village.

menu.title: Menu
menu.skillsHelp: Learn a skill from a trainer once, then use it freely. Focus it in battle for bonus power.

settings.timersHelp: Timed Focus puzzles (ninja and ranger skills) have a clock. Relaxed doubles the time, Off removes timers completely.
settings.tutorHelp: Owl the tutor runs on your own computer through Claude Code, Gemini CLI or Codex CLI. Install one of them, run "npm run tutor" in the game folder, and play the game from "npm run dev" on the same computer. Owl only gives hints and questions, never answers.

help.title: How to play
help.move: Move: click where you want to go (the dots show the path), or walk freely with WASD / the arrow keys. Up on the keyboard is up on the screen. Zoom with the mouse wheel or + and −. In battle, WASD pans the camera.
help.talk: Talk / examine: click a person or the rune gate. The party walks over and starts talking. (E also works when you stand next to them.)
help.menu: Menu: Esc · Quests: Q · Skills: K · Bag: I
help.combat1: Battle: each turn a character gains AP (Action Points). Moving costs 1 AP per 3 tiles, and skills show their AP cost.
help.combat2: Click a blue tile to move. Pick a skill with 1–4, then click a target.
help.combat3: ✦ Focus (F): charge a skill now, release it next turn with a puzzle. A right answer makes it much stronger and lets it pierce armor.
help.combat4: Space ends the turn. Right-click or Esc cancels a skill.
help.learn1: Learn once, cast many: trainers teach skills through a short trial.
help.learn2: Attunement: skills fade a little after each battle unless you release them with a right Focus answer. Practise with trainers to restore them.
help.learn3: Stuck? Use the Hint button. Every wrong answer shows the steps.
help.combat5: Height: higher ground gives +25% damage per level and +1 range for ranged skills. Climbing costs extra movement.
help.tutor: AI tutor: when the local tutor is running, untimed questions get an "Ask Owl" button. Owl asks guiding questions and never gives the answer.
help.combat6: Auto (Q): let a hero play their turn with learned skills only. Good for easy fights; hard enemies need Focus.
help.notebook: Notebook (N): write your own notes and working, and see the formulas you have learned. It is also inside every untimed puzzle.

elder.intro1: Kai, Aino, thank goodness you're here. The Riddle Golem sits on our spring, and no blade can cut its stone shell.
elder.intro2: Its shell is bound by a seal: a hidden number. Find the number and the seal shatters.
elder.intro3: Master Ren at the dojo teaches the ninja way: fast thinking, guess and check. Sage Lumi at the library teaches the mage way: equations that reveal the unknown.
elder.intro4: Learn what you can. The way to the ruins is long: first the forest clearing, then the marsh to the south, then the caves. Only when the caves are quiet will the rune gate wake.
elder.kaiReply: Fast thinking? Sounds like my kind of training.
elder.ainoReply: And mine is the slow, clever kind. We'll find that number, Elder.
elder.intro5: Oh, and Helmi at the farm could use a hand. Even heroes need bread.
elder.golem1: The golem's seals are equations. The first one is simple, but each time you break one, a harder one forms.
elder.golem2: Break its seals, strike while it is open, and the spring is ours again.
elder.hintTrain: You can't break a seal yet. Learn Probe Strike from Master Ren, or Unbind from Sage Lumi. Both is even better.
elder.hintGate: Go east, over the bridge and through the forest. The rune gate guards the ruins.
elder.hintGolem: The gate is open. The golem waits in the ruins. Be brave, and check your answers.
elder.thanks: The spring flows again! Numerola will remember you, Kai and Aino.
elder.hintForest: Start with the forest clearing east of the bridge. The slimes there are a good first fight.
elder.hintMarsh: The forest path south leads to the Times-Table Marsh. Frogs and splitting slimes live there.
elder.hintCaves: East of the marsh are the Echo Caves. Their beetles wear hard shells: Focus your attacks.

ren.busy: Hmph. Speak with Elder Vesa first, then come back.
ren.intro1: So, you want to learn the ninja way. A ninja does not stop to ponder. A ninja knows.
ren.intro2: Each technique starts with a trial. Pass it once and the move is yours. Practise it and it stays sharp.
ren.menuDone: You have learned all I teach. Keep your mind sharp.
ren.about1: Ninja moves cost little and strike fast. Focus one and I will throw quick questions at you when it fires. Answer before the timer runs out!
ren.about2: Probe Strike is guess and check: pick a number, test it on the seal, adjust. Slow? Maybe. But it always works.
ren.sealHint: Remember: against a seal, pick a number for x and calculate. Too small? Go bigger. Too big? Go smaller.

lumi.busy: Ah, visitors! Do talk to Elder Vesa first. He has news.
lumi.intro1: Welcome to the library. A mage's power comes from understanding, not speed.
lumi.intro2: My trials are untimed. Take your time, use hints, and learn to see the shape of a problem.
lumi.menuDone: You've mastered my lessons. The rest is practice.
lumi.about1: Mage spells are strong but cost more AP. Focus a spell and you solve a problem, with no timer, when it fires. Right answers make it far stronger.
lumi.about2: Unbind reads a seal like a balance scale. Whatever you do to one side, do to the other, until x stands alone.
lumi.sealHint: When you face the golem, cast Unbind and solve its equation. One correct answer breaks the seal.

flurry.intro: Flurry! Strike, strike, strike. To learn it, add and subtract quickly in your head. Four correct answers.
flurry.outro: In battle, Focus a Flurry: when it fires, every quick correct answer adds one more hit to the combo.

shadowStep.intro: Shadow Step. Times tables, student. A ninja knows them without counting. Four correct.
shadowStep.outro: Shadow Step costs only 1 AP. Use it to slip behind enemies or reach high ground.

probe.intro: Probe Strike. First, the order of operations: multiply before you add, unless brackets say otherwise.
probe.guess: Now the real lesson. This practice seal says 2x + 1 = 11. Pick a value for x, work out 2x + 1, and see if it makes 11.
probe.keepTrying: Giving up already? A ninja tries again. Pick another number.
probe.outro: Against a seal, Probe Strike lets you test one guess each time. Every miss tells you whether to go bigger or smaller.

fireball.intro: Fireball covers an area: a rectangle of burning ground. Let's learn to measure areas. Rows times columns. Three correct.
fireball.outro: Fireball burns a 3 × 3 area (9 tiles) and leaves flames for 2 rounds. Careful, it burns friends too! Focus it and solve an area question for a much bigger blast.

mend.intro: Mend heals by filling in what is missing. So: missing-number puzzles. What goes in the box? Four correct.
mend.outro: Focus Mend and solve a missing-number puzzle when it fires, and it heals far more.

unbind.intro: Unbind is the deepest lesson: the balance scale. A bag hides an unknown number of weights. Keep the scale level and find out how many.
unbind.stage1: One bag and 3 weights balance 7 weights. Take weights off, but always the same on both sides!
unbind.stage2: Two bags and 1 weight balance 9 weights. When only bags are left on one side, split both sides into equal groups.
unbind.stage3: Bags on both sides! You can take a bag off each side too, because a bag weighs the same everywhere.
unbind.symbols: Wonderful. Now the same thing without the scale, just symbols. x is the bag, and the numbers are weights.
unbind.outro: With Unbind, one correct answer shatters a seal. Picture the scale and it will help you think.

dash.intro: Vector Dash. A dash is a vector: so many steps right, so many up. Add two dashes and you add their parts. Three correct.
dash.outro: Now you can dash anywhere within 5 tiles for 1 AP.

vflurry.intro: Flurry, the Eigenvale way: dot products, fast. Multiply matching parts and add. Three correct.
vflurry.outro: Focus a Flurry and every quick dot product adds another hit.

eprobe.intro: Probe Strike against matrix seals. First, determinants: a·d − b·c. Two correct.
eprobe.guess: Now guess and check. This practice seal hides an eigenvalue λ. Pick a λ and work out det(A − λI). When it is zero, you found one.
eprobe.outro: Against a matrix seal, Probe Strike tests one λ each time. Hint: the eigenvalues add up to the trace and multiply to the determinant.

beam.intro: Matrix Beam. A matrix moves every point: each row of A dotted with v gives one part of Av. Three correct.
beam.outro: Matrix Beam hits a 3 × 3 area. Focus it and solve a matrix-vector product for a much stronger beam.

emend.intro: Mend scales life back up. Scaling a vector multiplies every part by the same number. Three correct.
emend.outro: Focus Mend and scale a vector when it fires to heal far more.

eunbind.intro: Unbind is the deepest lesson. Some vectors are only stretched by a matrix, never turned. Their stretch factors are the eigenvalues. First, a determinant.
eunbind.values: Now eigenvalues. Use the trace and the determinant: λ² − (trace)λ + det = 0. Two correct.
eunbind.vectors: Last, an eigenvector: subtract λ from the diagonal, then find a v that the new matrix sends to zero.
eunbind.outro: With Unbind, one correct answer shatters a matrix seal. The working steps help you, and they count.

aimed.intro: Aimed Shot. An archer reads directions with the dot product: multiply matching parts, then add. Three correct.
aimed.outro: Focus an Aimed Shot and solve a dot product when it fires: ×2.5 damage, straight through armor.

volley.intro: Volley. Each arrow’s flight is a vector, and you aim by adding vectors. Three correct.
volley.outro: Volley rains on a 3 × 3 area. Focus it and add vectors for a deadlier rain.

mark.intro: Mark. Two directions are perpendicular exactly when their dot product is 0. Find the dot products. Three correct.
mark.outro: A marked enemy takes 50% more damage for 2 turns.

ward.intro: Ward. A matrix scales area by its determinant: a·d − b·c. A shield is an area you can hide behind. Three correct.
ward.outro: Ward gives an ally a 10-point shield. Focus it and compute a determinant for a much thicker shield.

taunt.intro: Taunt. Make yourself big: scale a vector up. Two correct.
taunt.outro: Taunt forces enemies to attack Otso for 2 turns. Use it when a friend is hurt or focusing.

quake.intro: Quake. Multiplying matrices: each entry is a row of the first times a column of the second. Two correct.
quake.outro: Quake hits every enemy next to Otso. Focus it and multiply matrices for a ground-splitting quake.

cstep.intro: Lucky Step. Before you leap, know how far things spread: the range is the largest value minus the smallest. Three correct.
cstep.outro: Now you can step anywhere within 5 tiles for 1 AP.

cflurry.intro: Flurry, Chancewood style: chances, fast. Favourable outcomes divided by all outcomes. Three correct.
cflurry.outro: Focus a Flurry and every quick chance you work out adds another hit.

cprobe.intro: Lucky Strike. Luck favours the quick: first, two pouches of coins.
cprobe.seal: Now a practice seal. No working, just the answer, before the sand runs out.
cprobe.again: Not this time. Count again: what you want, out of everything.
cprobe.outro: Against a chance seal, Lucky Strike gives you one fast question. A fraction like 3/8, a decimal or a percent all count.

cstorm.intro: Average Storm. The mean is the fair share: add all the values, then divide by how many there are. Three correct.
cstorm.outro: Average Storm hits a 3 × 3 area. Focus it and work out a mean for a much bigger storm.

cmend.intro: Mend. The median is the middle value once you sort the list. Three correct.
cmend.outro: Focus Mend and find a median when it fires: it heals far more.

cunbind.intro: Unbind is the deepest lesson. Every chance is a fraction: favourable outcomes out of all outcomes. First, one draw.
cunbind.not: Now the opposite: the chance that something does NOT happen is 1 minus the chance that it does.
cunbind.two: Last, two things at once. If they do not affect each other, multiply their chances.
cunbind.outro: With Unbind you solve a chance seal step by step, with no timer. The working counts.

jinx.intro: Jinx. To jinx something, think of everything that is NOT what you want: 1 − P. Three correct.
jinx.outro: A jinxed enemy takes 50% more damage for 2 turns.

dice.intro: Dice Storm. Two dice have 6 × 6 = 36 outcomes. Count the ways to make a sum. Two correct.
dice.outro: Dice Storm hits a 3 × 3 area. Focus it and solve a dice question for a bigger storm.

fortune.intro: Fortune's Favour. Is a game worth playing? The expected value: chance to win × prize. Two correct.
fortune.outro: Fortune's Favour gives an ally a 10-point charm. Focus it and work out an expected value for a much stronger charm.

tstep.intro: Tide Step. Every right triangle has three sides: opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse. sin, cos and tan are ratios of them: SOH CAH TOA. Three correct.
tstep.outro: Now you can step anywhere within 5 tiles for 1 AP.

tflurry.intro: Flurry, Tidewatch style: turn the beam. Drag the Trig Lens until it shows the value asked. Three correct.
tflurry.outro: Focus a Flurry and turn the beam fast: every right angle adds another hit.

tprobe.intro: Tide Strike. Quick eyes first: two triangles.
tprobe.seal: Now a practice seal. No working, just the answer, before the tide turns.
tprobe.again: Not this time. sin is opposite over hypotenuse: half the hypotenuse at 30°.
tprobe.outro: Against a tide seal, Tide Strike gives you one fast question. Typing √3/2 or 0.866 both work.

twave.intro: Sine Wave. If you know an angle and the hypotenuse, the opposite side is hypotenuse × sin θ. Read sin θ off the Lens if you need to. Three correct.
twave.outro: Sine Wave hits a 3 × 3 area. Focus it and work out a side for a much bigger wave.

tmend.intro: Mend. On the unit circle the triangle’s sides are sin and cos, and the hypotenuse is 1. So sin² + cos² = 1, always. Two correct.
tmend.outro: Focus Mend and use sin² + cos² = 1 when it fires: it heals far more.

tunbind.intro: Unbind is the deepest lesson. The Tide Serpent’s seals are triangles, circles and identities. First, a side of a triangle.
tunbind.circle: Now the unit circle: past 90°, the beam points left or down, and sin or cos turn negative. Use the angle back to the x-axis, then the sign.
tunbind.outro: With Unbind you solve a tide seal step by step, with the Lens beside you. The working counts.

bearing.intro: Take Bearing. A navigator finds angles from sides: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, then turn the Lens until sin θ matches. Two correct.
bearing.outro: A marked enemy takes 50% more damage for 2 turns.

tide.intro: Tidal Wave. The tide is a sine wave: its amplitude is how high it goes, its period how long one wave takes. Three correct.
tide.outro: Tidal Wave hits a 3 × 3 area. Focus it and read a wave for a stronger tide.

beacon.intro: Beacon. Sailors measure angles in radians: half a turn, 180°, is π. Three correct.
beacon.outro: Beacon gives an ally a 10-point shield of light. Focus it and convert an angle for a stronger beacon.

pekka.busy: Shop's not open yet, friend. The Elder was looking for you!
pekka.hello: Welcome to Pekka's! Tonics, tea, seeds, all honestly priced. Mostly.
pekka.chat1: Business? Everyone counts their coins twice since the spring dried up.
pekka.chat2: Tip: if you can work out a discount in your head, I might just throw in something for free.

shop.badQty: Type a whole number, 1 or more.

shop.haggleLose: "Ha! Better luck next time, friend." (Pekka only haggles once.)

helmi.busy: Oh, hello! Have you seen the Elder? He's been asking for you.
helmi.intro1: Kai! Aino! Perfect timing. I need to sow my new field, but it's a crooked thing.
helmi.intro2: It's like a rectangle with a corner bitten off. I need 3 seeds for every square metre.
helmi.intro3: If I buy too few, part of it stays bare. Too many and I waste coins. Can you work out how much it needs?
helmi.ask: Will you help me plan the field?
helmi.later: No worries. The field isn't going anywhere.
helmi.comeBack: Come back whenever you're ready to finish the plan.
helmi.planned: {area} m², so {seeds} seeds! Pekka sells them in bags of {bag}. Could you buy what we need and bring it here?
helmi.needSeeds: We need {seeds} seeds. Pekka sells them in bags of {bag}.
helmi.short: You have {have} seeds, but the field needs {need}. That's {missing} short.
helmi.under: We planted what we could, about {pct}% of the field. It'll do, but a few rows stay bare.
helmi.over: All planted! Though... that's {extra} seeds too many, {bags} bag(s) you didn't need. Thanks anyway!
helmi.exact: Perfect! {bags} bags and only {left} seeds left over. You can't buy part of a bag, so that's spot on. Take these tonics too!
helmi.done: The field is growing. Thank you for your help!
helmi.doneExact: Look at those sprouts, every square metre covered. You're a natural farmer!

farm.title: Planning Helmi's field
farm.intro: Each square is 1 m². Helmi needs {rate} seeds per m². Choose any way to work out the area. They all give the same answer!
farm.qArea: What is the area of the field in m²?
farm.qSeeds: The field is {area} m². With {rate} seeds per m², how many seeds are needed?
farm.forgotCorner: That's the whole 8 × 6 rectangle, but a corner is missing!

hint.none: Try one of the ways to think above.
hint.count: Count every square inside the field. The numbers help.
hint.split: Find the areas of A and B separately, then add them.
hint.subtract: The big 8 × 6 rectangle, minus the missing 3 × 2 corner.

gate.locked: Runes glow on a sealed stone gate. A voice rumbles: "Only those who can find a hidden number may pass." (Learn Probe Strike or Unbind first.)
gate.intro: The runes on the gate glow, one number on each stone. There's a pattern...
gate.opened: The last rune flares and the gate grinds open. Cold air flows out of the ruins.
gate.foreshadow: Kai, did you see? The rule was 3 × n + 4, and 25 was on rune 7. I bet the golem's seals work the same way.
gate.lockedStages: The runes on the gate are dark and cold. The Elder said they would wake only when the forest, the marsh and the caves are quiet.

runes.title: The Rune Gate
runes.s1: Five rune stones. The last one has no number.
runes.h1: How much bigger is each rune than the one before?
runes.e1: Each rune is {d} more than the one before: {last} + {d} = {ans}.
runes.s2: Far down the wall, another rune lights up: rune #10.
runes.h2: Rune #1 is {m} × 1 + {a}. Rune #2 is {m} × 2 + {a}. See the rule?
runes.e2: The rule is {m} × position + {a}. So rune #10 is {m} × 10 + {a} = {ans}.
runes.s3: Now the gate asks the opposite question.
runes.h3: {m} × n + {a} = {v}. Undo the steps: take away {a}, then divide by {m}.

battle.forest1: Slimes! Watch out, Aino. They're made of loose numbers.
battle.golem2: NO BLADE CAN CUT ME. NO FIRE CAN BURN ME. ONLY THE HIDDEN NUMBER.
battle.golemAino: Look at the seal around it. It's an equation! Find x and it breaks.
battle.sealRule: While the golem is sealed, it takes no damage. Break the seal to make it vulnerable, and it also loses its next turn. When its health drops far enough, a new, harder seal forms.
battle.tipProbe: Kai, Probe Strike: guess a value for x and calculate. Too small or too big? Adjust and try again.
battle.tipUnbind: Aino, Unbind: solve the equation like a balance scale. One correct answer breaks the seal.
battle.marsh1: Careful, Kai: those frogs pull you in with their tongues, and that purple slime splits when it pops!
battle.marshTip1: Tongue Frogs pull heroes towards them. Splitter Slimes burst into two droplets when defeated.
battle.marshTip2: Fireball hits a 3 × 3 area: great against droplets standing together. Focus it and solve an area question for a bigger blast.
battle.caves1: Shell beetles! My strikes just bounce off that armor.
battle.cavesTip1: Shell Beetles have 2 armor: every learned hit loses 2 damage. Focused attacks pierce armor.
battle.cavesTip2: The Cave Shade mends its friends. Take it down first.

tutorial.title: Battle basics
tutorial.l1: Battles are turn-based on a grid. Each turn a character gains 4 Action Points (AP), and can save up to 6.
tutorial.l2: Click a blue tile to move (1 AP buys 3 tiles). Click an enemy next to you to attack. WASD pans the camera and the mouse wheel zooms.
tutorial.l3: Use number keys 1–4 or the buttons for skills. Each shows its AP cost. Some need a few turns to cool down.
tutorial.l4: Learned skills work without any math. For more power, select a skill and turn on ✦ Focus (F): you charge it now and solve a puzzle at the start of your next turn.
tutorial.l5: Press Space or End turn when you're done. Right-click or Esc cancels a skill.
tutorial.l6: Height matters. Attacks from higher ground deal more damage, and ranged skills reach 1 tile further. Climbing up costs extra movement, and you can only climb one level at a time.
tutorial.l7: In a hurry? Auto (Q) plays a hero’s turn with learned skills. But armored enemies shrug off learned attacks; only Focus pierces armor.

numerola.desc: Where every journey starts. Learn the game: skills, Focus, Auto, high ground. Sums, times tables, areas, missing numbers and first equations. Three areas, then the Riddle Golem.

eigenvale.tier: Linear algebra · upper secondary to university

chancewood.name: Chancewood

fluxreach.name: Fluxreach

bitforge.name: Bitforge
bitforge.desc: A city of gears and logic gates. Binary, logic, algorithms and complexity.

forcehold.name: Forcehold

tidewatch.name: Tidewatch

renEv.intro1: Kai! So you followed the warp to Eigenvale too. Good. Here, speed means vectors.
renEv.intro2: Same rules as at home: pass a trial once and the move is yours. Practise it and it stays sharp.
renEv.menuDone: You have learned all I teach here.
renEv.about1: A vector is just a list of steps: so many right, so many up. Add vectors by adding their parts.
renEv.about2: Probe Strike works on matrix seals too: guess λ, compute det(A − λI). Zero means you hit an eigenvalue.
renEv.sealHint: Against a matrix seal: guess a λ and compute det(A − λI). The eigenvalues add up to the trace, so guess near half of it.

kerttu.intro1: Aino, Lumi’s apprentice! Lumi taught you the balance scale. I teach you what a matrix does to space.
kerttu.intro2: My lessons have steps. Write each step down; the working is part of the answer.
kerttu.menuDone: You know my matrices now. Go unwarp the land.
kerttu.about1: A matrix moves every point of the plane. Look where it sends the two arrows of the unit square: those are its columns.
kerttu.about2: An eigenvector is a direction the matrix only stretches. The stretch factor is its eigenvalue λ: A v = λ v.
kerttu.sealHint: The Eigenwarden’s seals are matrices. Cast Unbind and find the eigenvalue, or later the eigenvector, step by step.

ilona.intro1: Sana, take the bow. Directions are everything for a ranger, and directions are vectors.
ilona.intro2: Your trials use the dot product. It tells how much two arrows point the same way.
ilona.menuDone: You shoot like a cartographer now.
ilona.about1: u · v = u₁v₁ + u₂v₂. Big and positive: same direction. Zero: perpendicular. Negative: opposite.
ilona.about2: Adding vectors is like walking one arrow, then the next: tip to tail.
ilona.sealHint: Keep your distance and mark the strongest foe first.

vera.intro1: Otso. A shieldbearer holds a line, and a matrix can squash or stretch a line. Learn which.
vera.intro2: Determinants first: how much a matrix scales area. Then matrix products.
vera.about1: det A = a·d − b·c. If it is 0, the matrix flattens space onto a line and can’t be undone.
vera.about2: Multiplying matrices: entry (i, j) is row i of the first times column j of the second.
vera.sealHint: Taunt when someone is focusing. Shield them while they think.

notebook.title: Notebook
notebook.placeholder: Write your steps and ideas here…
notebook.mineHelp: Your own page. Jot down working before you commit to an answer. It stays for the whole campaign, and Owl the tutor can read it.
notebook.noFormulas: Learn a skill to add its formula here.

d.add_sub: Order doesn’t matter when you {1|add}: {1|a} + {2|b} is {2|b} + {1|a}.
d.area: The {3|area} is the {1|width} times the {2|height}: rows times columns.
d.missing: Undo the {1|added number}: take it away from the {2|total}.
d.order_ops: Brackets first, then × and ÷, then + and −.
d.eq2: Take the {2|plain number} off both sides, then divide by the {1|number of x’s}.
d.vec_add: Add {1|u} and {2|v} part by part. Picture it tip to tail.
d.vec_scale: Multiply every part of {2|v} by the {1|scalar} c.
d.dot: Multiply matching parts of {1|u} and {2|v}, then add. Positive means they point roughly the same way.
d.perp: {1|u} and {2|v} are at a right angle exactly when u · v = 0.
d.mat_vec: Each row of {1|A} dotted with {2|v} gives one part of the result.
d.mat_mul: Entry {3|cᵢⱼ} = {1|row i of A} · {2|column j of B}.
d.det2: {1|Main diagonal} minus {2|other diagonal}. It is how much A scales area.
d.eigen_val: Solve for {3|λ} using the {4|trace} (a + d) and the {5|determinant}.
d.eigen_vec: Subtract {3|λ} on the diagonal of {1|A}, then find a {2|v} that it sends to zero.
d.stat_mean: Add up the {1|values} and divide by {2|how many} there are.
d.stat_median: Sort the list; the {1|middle value} is the median. With an even count, take the mean of the two middle values.
d.stat_range: The {1|largest} value minus the {2|smallest}: how spread out the data is.
d.prob_simple: {1|Favourable} outcomes divided by {2|all} outcomes. Always between 0 and 1.
d.prob_not: The chance of {4|not A} is 1 minus the chance of {3|A}.
d.prob_two: If {1|A} and {2|B} do not affect each other, multiply: {3|P(A and B)} = P(A) × P(B).
d.prob_dice: Count the {1|ways} to make the sum in the 6 × 6 table, out of {2|36}.
d.expect: The {1|chance to win} times the {2|prize}: what you win on average.
d.trig_ratio: In a right triangle: sin = {1|opposite} ÷ {3|hypotenuse}, cos = {2|adjacent} ÷ hypotenuse, tan = opposite ÷ adjacent.
d.trig_sides: {1|Opposite} = {3|hypotenuse} × sin θ, adjacent = hypotenuse × cos θ.
d.trig_angle: Work out sin θ = {1|opposite} ÷ {3|hypotenuse}, then turn the Lens until sin matches: that is θ.
d.unit_circle: The beam’s tip is at ({2|cos θ}, {1|sin θ}). Left of the lamp, cos is negative; below it, sin is negative.
d.radians: Half a turn, 180°, is {3|π} radians. Radians = degrees ÷ 180 × π.
d.pythag_id: The triangle in the unit circle has sides {1|sin} and {2|cos} and hypotenuse 1, so by Pythagoras sin² + cos² = 1.
d.waves: y = {1|A} sin({2|B}x): A is the height (amplitude), 360° ÷ B the length of one wave (period).
d.trig_drag: {1|sin θ} is how high the beam’s tip is; {2|cos θ} is how far across.

notebook.lensHelp: Drag the beam around the circle, or drag along the wave. Toggle the layers to see how sin, cos and tan are connected.

steps.plotCaption: Arrows use the same colours as the formula. The shaded shape is where the matrix sends the unit square.
steps.hover: Hover or tap a coloured term to see what it means.
steps.fillAnswer: Write your answer first (steps help, but are optional).

vec_add.title: Adding vectors
vec_add.text: To add {1|u} and {2|v}, add their matching parts. On the grid: walk along {1|u}, then along {2|v}; you end at {3|the sum w}.
vec_add.g1: The first vector. Each part says how far to go along one axis.
vec_add.g2: The second vector, drawn starting from the tip of u.
vec_add.g3: The sum: where you end up after both walks.
vec_add.hint: Add the first parts together, then the second parts.

vec_scale.title: Scaling a vector
vec_scale.text: Multiplying {2|v} by the {1|scalar} stretches it (or flips it if negative). Every part gets multiplied: that’s {3|the result}.
vec_scale.g1: A scalar: a plain number that stretches or shrinks.
vec_scale.g3: The stretched vector. Same line, different length.

dot.title: Dot product
dot.text: The {3|dot product} multiplies matching parts of {1|u} and {2|v} and adds them up. It measures how much the two arrows point the same way.
dot.g3: One number: positive if u and v point roughly the same way, zero if perpendicular, negative if opposite.
dot.hint: Multiply the first parts, multiply the second parts, then add.

perp.title: Perpendicular?
perp.text: {1|u} and {2|v} are perpendicular (at a right angle) exactly when their {3|dot product} is 0. Work it out.
perp.g3: Zero means a right angle between the arrows.
perp.yes: It is 0, so u and v are perpendicular.
perp.no: It is not 0, so u and v are not perpendicular.

mat_vec.title: Matrix × vector
mat_vec.text: The {1|matrix A} moves the {2|vector v} to a new place, {3|Av}. Each part of {3|Av} is one row of {1|A} dotted with {2|v}.
mat_vec.g1: The matrix: a rule that moves every point. Its columns show where the two unit arrows go.
mat_vec.hint: Row 1 of A times v (multiply matching parts and add) gives the first part.
mat_vec.ex: Each row dotted with v: Av = {w}.

mat_mul.title: Matrix × matrix
mat_mul.text: Multiplying {1|A} by {2|B} means doing B, then A. Each entry of {3|C} is a row of {1|A} dotted with a column of {2|B}.
mat_mul.g1: The left matrix: use its rows.
mat_mul.g2: The right matrix: use its columns.
mat_mul.g3: The product. Entry cᵢⱼ uses row i of A and column j of B.
mat_mul.hint: c₁₁ = (row 1 of A) · (column 1 of B). Then the other three the same way.

det2.title: Determinant
det2.text: The {3|determinant} says how much the matrix scales area: the unit square becomes the shaded shape. It is the {1|main diagonal} minus the {2|other diagonal}.
det2.g3: The area scale. Negative means the shape is flipped; zero means it is squashed flat and can’t be undone.
det2.hint: Multiply the main diagonal, multiply the other diagonal, subtract.

eigen_val.title: Eigenvalues
eigen_val.text: Some vectors {2|v} are only stretched by {1|A}, never turned: {1|A}{2|v} = {3|λ}{2|v}. The stretch factors {3|λ} solve λ² − {4|trace}·λ + {5|det} = 0.
eigen_val.g2: An eigenvector: a direction that A keeps on its own line.
eigen_val.g3: An eigenvalue: how much A stretches that direction.
eigen_val.g4: The trace: the sum of the diagonal, a + d. The eigenvalues add up to it.
eigen_val.g5: The determinant, ad − bc. The eigenvalues multiply to it.
eigen_val.hint: Find two numbers that add up to the trace and multiply to the determinant.
eigen_val.ex2: λ² − {t}λ + {D} = 0 has the roots λ = {l1} and λ = {l2} (they add to {t} and multiply to {D}).

eigen_vec.title: Eigenvector
eigen_vec.text: For the eigenvalue {3|λ = {l}}, subtract it from the diagonal of {1|A} (that’s λ times the {4|identity I}). Then find a {2|direction v} that this new matrix sends to {6|zero}.
eigen_vec.g2: The eigenvector: any non-zero multiple counts.
eigen_vec.g4: The identity matrix: 1s on the diagonal. λI has λ on the diagonal.
eigen_vec.g6: The zero vector. (A − λI) squashes the eigenvector to nothing.
eigen_vec.hint: In A − λI, the first row says: (first entry)·v₁ + (second entry)·v₂ = 0. Pick v to make that true.
eigen_vec.ex2: One eigenvector is v = {v} (any multiple works).

eseal.probeValue: The seal is the matrix A = {m}. Guess an eigenvalue λ (a whole number).
eseal.wholeLambda: Pick a whole number between −20 and 20.
eseal.probeText: If {3|λ = {l}} is an eigenvalue, then {1|A} − λ{4|I} squashes space flat, so its determinant is 0.
eseal.probeHint: Subtract λ from a and from d, multiply them, then subtract b·c.
eseal.logHit: λ = {l}: det(A − λI) = 0. It is an eigenvalue!
eseal.missTip: Try another λ. The two eigenvalues add up to {tr} (the trace) and multiply to {det} (the determinant).
eseal.probeVector: The seal is A = {m}. Its eigenvalue is λ = {l}. Guess an eigenvector v = (v₁, v₂) with whole numbers.
eseal.probeVecText: If v is an eigenvector, then {1|A}{2|v} is just {3|{l}}·{2|v}: same direction, stretched.
eseal.logVecHit: v = {v}: Av = λv. It is an eigenvector!
eseal.vecTip: Try another direction. Look at the first row of A − λI: it must give 0.
eseal.unbindStory: The seal is a matrix. Work through the steps; the colours link each part of the formula to its meaning.

intro.p1: Beyond the mountains lies Eigenvale, a land of straight roads and perfect angles.
intro.p2: But the Eigenwarden has woken in the high spire. Its matrices warp the land: roads stretch, fields shear, and the maps are all wrong.
intro.p3: Kai and Aino followed the warp here. They meet Sana the ranger and Otso the shieldbearer. Cartographer Ilona is waiting in the town of Origin.

obj.talkIlona: Talk to Ilona, the cartographer, in Origin.
obj.plains: Go east and clear the Vector Plains (stage 1).
obj.mines: Take the road south and clear the Matrix Mines (stage 2).
obj.train: Learn Probe Strike (Ren) or Unbind (Archmage Kerttu) to break matrix seals.
obj.door: Open the Determinant Door below the Eigen Spire (east).
obj.warden: Climb the spire and break the Eigenwarden’s seals.
obj.survey0: Ilona needs help surveying the warp.
obj.glacier: Follow the icy path south-east to the Shear Glacier (stage 3).

main.title: The Warped Map
main.desc: The Eigenwarden’s matrices are warping Eigenvale.

survey.title: The Survey
survey.desc: Work out where the warp sends Ilona’s landmarks.

ilona.intro1: Travellers! You’re just in time. Look at my map: every road bends the wrong way.
ilona.intro2: The Eigenwarden in the spire is doing it. Its matrices move every point of the land, stretching some directions and turning others.
ilona.intro3: The spire is sealed behind the Determinant Door, and the Warden is wrapped in matrix seals. Only someone who can find eigenvalues gets through.
ilona.kai: Matrices? Sounds like Numerola’s equations, but bigger.
ilona.sana: I’ll come. I know the plains, and the wisps out there.
ilona.otso: And I’ll keep you all in one piece.
ilona.intro4: Train first: Ren, Archmage Kerttu, Captain Vera, and I’ll teach Sana myself. Then clear the plains and the mines.
ilona.thanks: My map is straight again. Thank you!
ilona.warden1: Its seals are matrices. Each hides an eigenvalue: a direction it only stretches. Find the stretch factor and the seal breaks.
ilona.warden2: Its second seal asks for the eigenvector itself, the direction. Its last seal is harder still.
ilona.survey1: The warp moves each landmark by a matrix. If I know where a landmark was, A times its position tells me where it is now.
ilona.survey2: Can you work out two of them for me?
ilona.surveyStory: A landmark at position v has been warped by the matrix A. Where is it now?
ilona.surveyRetry: Hmm, those don’t match my readings. Let’s try again later.

ren.busy: Kai! Speak with Ilona first, she knows what is going on.

kerttu.busy: Lumi’s apprentice? Find Ilona first, then come back to me.

door.lockedAreas: A great door of stone, with three matrices carved into it. It won’t budge. (Clear the Vector Plains, the Matrix Mines and the Shear Glacier first.)
door.lockedSkill: The matrices glow, but you can’t read them yet. (Learn Probe Strike or Unbind first.)
door.intro1: Three locks, three matrices. A voice echoes: “Only a matrix that can be undone may open me.”
door.intro2: A matrix can be undone exactly when its determinant is not 0. Compute all three.
door.which: Which lock’s matrix can be undone?
door.wrong: The lock grinds and stays shut. Its determinant is 0: it squashes space flat, so it can’t be undone.
door.opened: The lock turns, and the Determinant Door swings open. Stairs lead up into the spire.
door.aino: Determinant not zero: nothing gets squashed flat. Remember that, the Warden’s seals are next.

battle.plains1: Wisps! They zip around and blink away. And those slimes keep growing, so take them down fast.
battle.mines1: Crystal Golems. Armor thick as a wall, and they bite back. Learned attacks barely scratch them.
battle.minesTip1: Crystal Golems have 4 armor: every learned hit loses 4 damage, and they reflect 2 damage back. Focused attacks pierce armor and are not reflected.
battle.minesTip2: Use Otso’s Taunt and Ward to protect whoever is focusing. Shear Bats heal by biting, so take them out early.
battle.warden1: YOU WALK STRAIGHT LINES IN MY WARPED LAND?
battle.warden2: EVERY DIRECTION BENDS TO ME… EXCEPT THE ONES I ONLY STRETCH.
battle.wardenAino: The seal is a matrix! Find its eigenvalue and it breaks.
battle.sealRule: While sealed, the Eigenwarden takes no damage. Break the seal to make it vulnerable (and lose a turn). At 70 and 35 HP a new seal forms. It also has 3 armor, so Focus your big attacks.
battle.tipProbe: Kai, Probe Strike: guess λ, compute det(A − λI). For the vector seal, guess v and compute Av.
battle.tipUnbind: Aino, Unbind: trace and determinant first, then λ. For the vector seal: A − λI, then v.
battle.tipPush: Its Stretch attack shoves heroes away. Keep Otso in front.
battle.glacier1: The Shear Glacier. Ice sentries, frost wraiths, and a knight sealed in a matrix.
battle.glacierTip1: Ice Sentries gain 1 armor every turn (up to 4). Defeat them early, or pierce them with Focus.
battle.glacierTip2: Frost Wraiths chill whoever they hit: that hero has 2 less AP on their next turn.
battle.glacierTip3: The Frost Knight is sealed by a triangular matrix. For a triangular matrix the eigenvalues sit on the diagonal. Probe Strike or Unbind breaks the seal: a preview of the Eigenwarden.

tutorial.l1: Four heroes now: Kai, Aino, Sana and Otso. Each has a learned basic attack.
tutorial.l2: Auto (Q) plays a hero’s turn with learned skills. Easy fights go quickly this way.
tutorial.l3: ✦ Focus (F): select a skill, turn on Focus, pick a target. It charges now and fires at the start of your next turn after a puzzle. Right = ×2.5 and pierces armor.
tutorial.l4: The working counts: in step puzzles every right step adds power even if the final answer slips.
tutorial.l5: Open the Notebook inside any puzzle to write steps or look up formulas.

win.plains: The wisps fade and the slimes stop growing. The plains’ roads are straight again.
win.mines: The crystals crack and the bats scatter. In the rubble you find a Focus Tea.
win.warden: The last seal breaks. The Eigenwarden’s matrix becomes the identity, and the land snaps back into straight lines.
win.glacier: The sentries crack, the wraiths melt, and the Frost Knight bows. With all three lands quiet, the Determinant Door hums in the east.

ending.title: Eigenvale is straight again!
ending.p1: The Eigenwarden kneels, its matrix calm. Roads run true and Ilona’s map finally matches the land.
ending.p2: You learned that a matrix moves space, a determinant measures area, and eigenvectors are the directions that only stretch.
ending.p3: Next step for the curious: diagonalisation, Markov chains and PageRank. They all use the same idea.

renCh.intro1: Kai! You came to Chancewood too? Here, even a ninja must think about luck.
renCh.intro2: Same rules as always: pass a trial once and the move is yours.
renCh.menuDone: You have learned all I teach here.
renCh.about1: A chance is a fraction: the outcomes you want, divided by all the outcomes.
renCh.about2: Lucky Strike is fast: no working, just the answer. Fractions, decimals and percents all work.
renCh.sealHint: Madame Fortuna's seals ask for a chance. Count what you want, count everything, divide.

tilda.intro1: Aino, a fellow thinker! People here trust their luck. I trust my notebook.
tilda.intro2: Write the numbers down, sort them, add them. Data tells the truth when luck lies.
tilda.about1: Mean: add everything, divide by how many. Median: sort, take the middle. Range: largest minus smallest.
tilda.about2: P(not A) = 1 − P(A). And for two things that do not affect each other, P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
tilda.sealHint: With Unbind you can count the outcomes slowly and carefully. A table of two dice helps.

hannu.intro1: Onni, my boy! Come, sit. A real gambler never guesses: he counts.
hannu.intro2: I teach the dice. Learn the odds and luck becomes a tool.
hannu.menuDone: You know the odds better than me now, lad.
hannu.about1: Two dice: 36 outcomes. Only one way to roll 2, but six ways to roll 7. That is why 7 comes up so often.
hannu.about2: Expected value: what you win on average. A game is fair when it equals what you pay.
hannu.sealHint: Jinx the strongest foe, and charm whoever is focusing.

ev.even: a die shows an even number

cap.bars: One bar per value, in the order given.
cap.tokens: Every coin in the pouch. Colours match the formula.
cap.dice: Every outcome of the dice. The lit squares are the favourable ones.

stat_mean.title: Mean
stat_mean.text: Data: {data}. The {3|mean} is the fair share: add up the {1|sum} of all values, then divide by the {2|count} of values.
stat_mean.g3: The mean: what each would get if shared equally.
stat_mean.hint: Add all the numbers first. Then count them and divide.

stat_median.title: Median
stat_median.text: Data: {data}. Sort it from {2|smallest} to largest. The {3|median} is the {1|middle value}.
stat_median.g1: The position in the middle of the sorted list: (count + 1) ÷ 2.
stat_median.g3: The median: half the values are below it, half above.
stat_median.hint: Write the values in order. With 5 values, the 3rd is the middle.
stat_median.hintEven: Write the values in order. With 6 values, take the mean of the 3rd and the 4th.

stat_range.title: Range
stat_range.text: Data: {data}. The {3|range} shows how spread out the data is: the {1|largest} value minus the {2|smallest}.
stat_range.g3: The spread from bottom to top.
stat_range.hint: Find the largest and the smallest, then subtract.

prob_simple.title: Probability
prob_simple.text: A pouch holds {gold} gold coins and {other} copper coins. You pick one without looking. The {1|favourable} outcomes are the gold ones; the {2|total} is every coin. {3|P(gold)} = favourable ÷ total.
prob_simple.g3: The probability: a number from 0 (never) to 1 (always).
prob_simple.hint: Count the gold coins, count all the coins, and write a fraction.

prob_not.title: Not
prob_not.text: A pouch holds {gold} gold coins and {other} copper coins. What is the chance of {4|not} picking gold? It is 1 minus {3|P(gold)}.
prob_not.hint: First P(gold) as a fraction. Then take it away from 1.

prob_two.title: Two events
prob_two.text: {1|A}: {a}. {2|B}: {b}. They do not affect each other, so {3|P(A and B)} = P(A) × P(B).
prob_two.hint: Write each chance as a fraction, then multiply the tops and the bottoms.

prob_dice.title: Dice
prob_dice.text: Roll two dice. What is the chance that the sum is {s}? Count the {1|ways} to make {s} in the table, out of all {2|36} outcomes.
prob_dice.textOne: Roll one die. What is the chance of rolling {k} or more? Count the {1|ways}, out of {2|6} faces.
prob_dice.g1: The outcomes that give what we want.
prob_dice.g2one: A die has 6 equally likely faces.
prob_dice.hint: Look at the lit squares in the picture and count them.

expect.title: Expected value
expect.text: Roll a die. On {ways} of the 6 faces you win {prize} gold, otherwise nothing. The {3|expected value} is the {1|chance to win} times the {2|prize}.
expect.textCost: It costs {cost} gold to play. Roll a die: on {ways} of the 6 faces you win {prize} gold. The {3|expected value} is the {1|chance to win} times the {2|prize}, minus the {4|cost}.
expect.g1: The chance of winning, as a fraction.
expect.g3: What you win on average, per game.
expect.g4: What it costs to play once.
expect.hint: P(win) = winning faces ÷ 6. Then multiply by the prize.

cseal.title: Fortuna's seal
cseal.dice7: Two dice. What is the chance that they add up to 7? Count the {1|ways} in the table, out of {2|36}.
cseal.coins: Flip two coins. What is the chance of at least one heads? Easier the other way round: {3|no heads} means tails and tails. Then {4|at least one heads} = 1 − P(no heads).
cseal.coinsHint: P(tails) is 1/2. Multiply for two coins, then take it away from 1.
cseal.coinsEx: P(no heads) = 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4, so P(at least one heads) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.
cseal.probeStory: Lucky Strike: no working, just the answer. Quick!
cseal.unbindStory: The seal asks for a chance. Count carefully, step by step.

intro.p1: North of Numerola lies Chancewood, a forest where every path forks and every coin is tossed.
intro.p2: Madame Fortuna runs a carnival on the hill. Her wheel has been rigged, and now luck itself goes wrong: dice roll sevens all day, and coins never land the same way twice.
intro.p3: Kai and Aino arrive in the village of Fortune’s Rest. A lucky boy called Onni joins them. Tilda, who counts everything, is waiting.

obj.talkTilda: Talk to Tilda, the counter of things, in Fortune’s Rest.
obj.done: Luck is fair again in Chancewood!
obj.glade: Go east and clear the Coinflip Glade (stage 1).
obj.hollow: Take the road south and clear the Dice Hollow (stage 2).
obj.maze: Follow the path south-east into the Gambler's Maze (stage 3).
obj.train: Learn Lucky Strike (Ren) or Unbind (Tilda) to break chance seals.
obj.gate: Open the Wheel Gate below the carnival (east).
obj.fortuna: Climb to the carnival and break Madame Fortuna's seals.
obj.log0: Tilda wants help with her mushroom log.

main.title: The Rigged Wheel
main.desc: Madame Fortuna's rigged wheel has made luck itself unfair.

log.title: The Mushroom Log
log.desc: Help Tilda sum up a week of mushroom counts.
log.s1: Find the mean and the median

tilda.intro1: Visitors! Good. Everyone here blames luck. I count things instead.
tilda.intro2: Madame Fortuna rigged her great wheel, and since then chance itself is crooked. Imps flip coins at travellers, dice roll themselves, bandits cheat.
tilda.intro3: Her carnival is sealed behind the Wheel Gate, and she hides behind seals of chance. Only someone who can work out a probability gets through.
tilda.onni: I’ll come! I never lose at dice. Well... almost never.
tilda.kai: "Almost never" sounds like a probability to me.
tilda.intro4: Exactly. Train first: Ren is here, old Hannu teaches Onni, and I teach Aino. Then the glade, the hollow and the maze.
tilda.thanks: Fair chances again. My numbers thank you!
tilda.fortuna1: Her seals are questions of chance: a pouch of coins, two dice, two coins.
tilda.fortuna2: Answer one and the seal breaks. Each new seal is a little harder than the last.
tilda.log1: I count the mushrooms behind my house every day. Here is a week.
tilda.log2: What is a typical day? Work out the mean and the median for me.
tilda.logStory: Mushrooms per day for one week: {data}.
tilda.logRetry: Hmm, my notebook says otherwise. Let’s try again later.
tilda.logDone: That matches my notebook. The mean and the median are different, see? One big day pulls the mean up.
tilda.logAino: So the median is the "typical day", and the mean is the fair share.

hannu.busy: Speak with Tilda first, young ones.

ren.busy: Kai! Talk to Tilda first, she knows what is going on.

gate.lockedAreas: A gate shaped like a great spinner, with three wheels on it. It won’t turn. (Clear the Coinflip Glade, the Dice Hollow and the Gambler’s Maze first.)
gate.lockedSkill: The wheels glow, but you can’t read their odds yet. (Learn Lucky Strike or Unbind first.)
gate.intro1: Three wheels, each with some gold slices. A voice purrs: "Spin the luckiest wheel, and I open."
gate.intro2: Work out each wheel’s chance of landing on gold, then pick the best one.
gate.wheelText: This wheel has {all} equal slices, and {gold} of them are gold. The chance of gold is the {1|gold slices} out of {2|all slices}.
gate.cap: Every slice on the wheel. Colours match the formula.
gate.wheelStory: Work out the chance of gold for this wheel.
gate.which: Which wheel has the best chance of gold?
gate.wrong: The wheel spins... and stops on copper. {f} is not the biggest chance. Compare the fractions again.
gate.opened: The wheel lands on gold. Click, click, click: the Wheel Gate swings open. Music drifts down from the carnival.
gate.onni: 1/3 beats 1/4! Even I know that one.

battle.glade1: Coin Imps! They flip a coin every time you swing. Heads, they dodge.
battle.gladeTip1: Three heroes now: Kai, Aino and Onni. Onni throws coins from range.
battle.gladeTip2: Coin Imps dodge learned attacks half the time: P(dodge) = 1/2. A focused attack never misses.
battle.gladeTip3: Auto (Q) still works, but expect about half your learned hits to miss.
battle.hollow1: Dice Cubes. Their hits are a roll of two dice: anything from 2 to 12.
battle.hollowTip1: A Dice Cube hits for the sum of two dice. 7 is the most likely sum (6 ways out of 36), 2 and 12 the least (1 way each).
battle.hollowTip2: The Lucky Mimic has 3 armor, and on a 6 (a 1 in 6 chance) its bite does double damage. Focus to pierce its armor.
battle.maze1: Bandits and a joker. Careful, he shuffles us around!
battle.mazeTip1: Odds Bandits stab up close or throw knives from range, and a 6 doubles their damage.
battle.mazeTip2: The Joker swaps two heroes after its turn. Take it down first, or keep your healer away from it.
battle.fortuna1: STEP RIGHT UP! EVERY GAME IS FAIR... FOR ME.
battle.fortuna2: MY SEALS ASK ONE QUESTION: DO YOU KNOW YOUR CHANCES?
battle.fortunaOnni: Her seals are probability questions! Work them out and they break.
battle.sealRule: While sealed, Madame Fortuna takes no damage. Break a seal to make her vulnerable (and lose a turn). At 70 and 35 HP a new seal forms. She has 2 armor, and her hits can roll a lucky 6.
battle.tipProbe: Kai, Lucky Strike: one fast question, no working. Fractions like 3/8 work.
battle.tipUnbind: Aino, Unbind: count the favourable outcomes and all the outcomes, step by step.

win.glade: The imps run out of coins and vanish. The glade is quiet; a path opens south.
win.hollow: The dice stop rolling and crumble into pips. In a mimic’s mouth you find a Focus Tea.
win.maze: The bandits flee and the joker folds like a card. With all three areas safe, the Wheel Gate begins to turn by itself.
win.fortuna: The last seal breaks. Madame Fortuna’s wheel spins true again: every slice the same size.

ending.title: Luck is fair again!
ending.p1: Madame Fortuna bows and fixes her wheel. Coins land heads half the time, dice roll every number, and Onni still wins... sometimes.
ending.p2: You learned to sum up data with the mean, the median and the range, and to measure chance: favourable out of all, "not", two events at once, dice and fair games.
ending.p3: Next step for the curious: tree diagrams, conditional probability, and the normal distribution.

renTw.intro1: Kai! The sea air suits you. Here, speed means turning the beam to the right angle, fast.
renTw.intro2: Same rules as always: pass a trial once and the move is yours.
renTw.menuDone: You have learned all I teach here.
renTw.about1: SOH CAH TOA: sin is Opposite over Hypotenuse, cos is Adjacent over Hypotenuse, tan is Opposite over Adjacent.
renTw.about2: Open the Trig Lens in your notebook (N) and drag the beam. Watch the purple side: that is sin.
renTw.sealHint: The Serpent’s seals ask for a side, a value on the circle, or an identity. Answer fast with Tide Strike.

keeper.intro1: Aino, is it? My lamp went dark when the Serpent came. While it’s out, let me teach you what a beam really is.
keeper.intro2: The beam is a line of length 1 turning around a point. Where its tip is, across and up: that is cos and sin.
keeper.menuDone: You understand the light now as well as I do.
keeper.about1: The tip of the beam is at (cos θ, sin θ). Drag it in the Trig Lens and the sine wave unrolls beside it.
keeper.about2: Turn the beam past 90° and cos goes negative, the tip is left of the lamp. Past 180°, sin goes negative too.
keeper.sealHint: With Unbind you can work slowly, with the Lens beside you. Use the reference angle, then the sign.

aava.intro1: Meri, you’ve found some friends. Good. A navigator never sails alone.
aava.intro2: I’ll teach you bearings, waves and radians. The sea speaks in angles.
aava.menuDone: You can navigate by yourself now, Meri.
aava.about1: A wave y = A sin(Bx): A is how high, 360° ÷ B is how long one wave is.
aava.about2: Radians measure angles by arc length: walk one radius along the circle and you have turned 1 radian. Half a turn is π.
aava.sealHint: Take a bearing on the strongest foe, and keep the beacon on whoever is focusing.

lens.aria: Trig Lens: drag to turn the beam, or use the arrow keys
lens.help: Drag the beam or the wave. Arrow keys: 1°, with Shift: 15°.
lens.title: Turn the beam

task.sin: Turn the beam until sin θ = {v}, with θ between {lo}° and {hi}°.
task.cos: Turn the beam until cos θ = {v}, with θ between {lo}° and {hi}°.
task.tan: Turn the beam until tan θ = {v}, with θ between {lo}° and {hi}°.

hint.sin: sin θ is how HIGH the beam’s tip is. Above the centre it is positive, below it negative.
hint.cos: cos θ is how far the tip is to the RIGHT. Left of the centre it is negative.
hint.tan: Turn on the tan wall: tan θ is how high the beam hits the wall one radius away.

ex.sin: At {a}° the tip is at height {v}: sin {a}° = {v}.
ex.cos: At {a}° the tip is {v} across: cos {a}° = {v}.
ex.tan: At {a}° the beam hits the wall at height {v}: tan {a}° = {v}.

g.opposite: The side across from the angle θ.
g.adjacent: The side next to the angle θ (not the hypotenuse).
g.hypotenuse: The longest side, across from the right angle.
g.theta: The angle we turn, measured from the right-hand x-axis, anticlockwise.
g.sinCircle: sin θ: how high the tip of the beam is.
g.cosCircle: cos θ: how far right the tip of the beam is.
g.tan: tan θ: how high the beam hits the wall one radius away (= sin ÷ cos).
g.radian: π radians = half a turn. One radian is the angle whose arc is one radius long.
g.amplitude: How high the wave goes above the middle.

cap.triangle: The triangle. Colours match the formula.
cap.lens: The Trig Lens is set to this angle. Read sin, cos or tan from it (drag to explore, Reset to come back).
cap.find: Turn the beam until sin θ matches your value; then read θ.
cap.circle: The beam at this angle. Drag to explore; the numbers are hidden on purpose.
cap.arc: The pink arc is the angle in radians: its length counted in radii.
cap.wave: The wave over one full turn, 0° to 360°.

trig_ratio.title: SOH CAH TOA

text.sin: A right triangle has sides {o}, {a} and {h}. From the angle θ, the {1|opposite} side is {o} and the {3|hypotenuse} is {h}. sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse.
text.cos: A right triangle has sides {o}, {a} and {h}. From the angle θ, the {2|adjacent} side is {a} and the {3|hypotenuse} is {h}. cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse.
text.tan: A right triangle has sides {o}, {a} and {h}. From the angle θ, the {1|opposite} side is {o} and the {2|adjacent} side is {a}. tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent.

trig_ratio.hint: Find the two sides in the picture, then write them as a fraction.

trig_sides.title: A side from an angle

text.sin: A ladder of length {known} (the {3|hypotenuse}) leans at {angle}°. How high does it reach (the {1|opposite} side)? Opposite = hypotenuse × sin θ.
text.cos: A rope of length {known} (the {3|hypotenuse}) is pegged at {angle}°. How far along the ground is the peg (the {2|adjacent} side)? Adjacent = hypotenuse × cos θ.
text.tan: You stand {known} m from a mast (the {2|adjacent} side) and look up at {angle}°. How tall is the mast (the {1|opposite} side)? Opposite = adjacent × tan θ.

trig_sides.hint: Read the sin, cos or tan of the angle from the Lens, then multiply.
trig_sides.hintSpecial: sin 30° = 1/2 and cos 60° = 1/2: the side is half of the hypotenuse.

trig_angle.title: An angle from sides
trig_angle.text: A rope {hyp} m long (the {3|hypotenuse}) holds a mast top {opp} m high (the {1|opposite} side). What is the angle θ? First sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, then turn the Lens until sin θ matches.
trig_angle.hint: Divide, then drag the beam until the purple side (sin) shows the same number. Read θ.

unit_circle.title: The unit circle

text.sin: Turn the beam to {angle}°. What is {1|sin} {angle}°? Use the {5|angle} back to the x-axis (a value you know), then decide the sign: is the tip above or below the centre?
text.cos: Turn the beam to {angle}°. What is {2|cos} {angle}°? Use the {5|angle} back to the x-axis (a value you know), then decide the sign: is the tip left or right of the centre?

unit_circle.hint: sin 30° = 1/2, sin 45° = √2/2 ≈ 0.707, sin 60° = √3/2 ≈ 0.866 (and cos is the other way round). Then pick the sign from the picture.
unit_circle.ex: The angle to the x-axis is {ref}°, and the picture gives the sign: {fn} {angle}° = {v}.

radians.title: Radians
radians.text: Write {d}° in radians, as a fraction of {3|π}. Half a turn, 180°, is π radians.
radians.textBack: Write {n}π/{m} radians in degrees. {3|π} radians is 180°.
radians.hint: Divide the degrees by 180: that is how many π.
radians.hintBack: Replace π with 180°, then work out the fraction.

pythag_id.title: sin² + cos² = 1
pythag_id.text: An angle θ (less than 90°) has sin θ = {o}/{h}. Find cos θ. On the unit circle {1|sin² θ} + {2|cos² θ} = 1.
pythag_id.textTan: An angle θ (less than 90°) has sin θ = {o}/{h}. Find tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ. First use {1|sin² θ} + {2|cos² θ} = 1 to find cos θ.
pythag_id.hint: Square sin θ, take it away from 1, then take the square root.
pythag_id.hintTan: Find cos θ first with sin² + cos² = 1, then divide sin by cos.
pythag_id.ex: It is the {o}-{a}-{h} triangle: sin = {o}/{h}, cos = {a}/{h}, tan = {o}/{a}.

waves.title: Waves
waves.text: The tide follows y = {A} · sin({B}x). How high does it rise above the middle? That is the {1|amplitude}.
waves.textPeriod: The tide follows y = {A} · sin({B}x). How many degrees does one whole wave take? That is the {2|period}: 360° ÷ {B}.
waves.hint: Look at the highest point of the graph.
waves.hintPeriod: Count the waves in 360°, or divide 360° by the number in front of x.
waves.ex: The highest point is {A}: the amplitude is {A}.

tseal.title: Tide seal
tseal.ladder: A {hyp} m mast leans at 30° to the water. How high does its top reach? The {1|opposite} side = {3|hypotenuse} × sin 30°.
tseal.circle: The beam turns to 120°. What is {2|cos} 120°? The tip is left of the centre, so cos is negative.
tseal.identity: An angle has {1|sin θ} = 3/5 (θ less than 90°). What is {4|tan θ}? First {2|cos θ} from sin² + cos² = 1.
tseal.probeStory: Tide Strike: no working, just the answer. Quick!
tseal.unbindStory: The seal is a question about angles. Work through the steps; the Lens is beside you.

intro.p1: South of Numerola the land ends at the sea. Here, in Tidewatch, the lighthouse beam turns all night and the tides rise and fall like clockwork.
intro.p2: But the Tide Serpent has coiled around Lighthouse Rock. The lamp is dark, the tides have lost their rhythm, and ships run aground.
intro.p3: Kai and Aino reach Lantern Cove. Meri, a young navigator, joins them. Keeper Vilho is waiting by his cold lamp.

obj.talkKeeper: Talk to Keeper Vilho in Lantern Cove.
obj.done: The lighthouse shines and the tides are back in rhythm!
obj.pools: Go east and clear the Tidepools (stage 1).
obj.cliffs: Take the cliff path south and clear the Gull Cliffs (stage 2).
obj.reef: Follow the path south-east to the Shipwreck Reef (stage 3).
obj.train: Learn Tide Strike (Ren) or Unbind (Keeper Vilho) to break tide seals.
obj.gate: Open the Beacon Gate below Lighthouse Rock (east).
obj.serpent: Climb Lighthouse Rock and break the Tide Serpent’s seals.
obj.survey0: Keeper Vilho wants the lighthouse measured.

main.title: The Dark Lighthouse
main.desc: The Tide Serpent has put out the lamp and broken the rhythm of the tides.
main.s1: Meet Keeper Vilho in Lantern Cove

survey.title: How Tall Is the Lighthouse?
survey.desc: Measure the lighthouse with an angle and a distance.

keeper.intro1: Travellers, at last. Forty years I’ve kept this light, and never has it been this dark.
keeper.intro2: The Tide Serpent wrapped itself around Lighthouse Rock. Since then the tides come whenever they like, not in their old smooth rhythm.
keeper.intro3: The Rock is closed by the Beacon Gate, and the Serpent hides behind seals of angles. Only someone who understands sin, cos and tan gets through.
keeper.meri: I’ll guide you! I’m Meri, Captain Aava’s navigator. I steer by angles.
keeper.aino: Sin and cos always felt like magic numbers to me. I’d like to finally see where they come from.
keeper.intro4: Then look through the Trig Lens: open your notebook and turn the beam. Train with Ren, Captain Aava and me. Then the pools, the cliffs and the reef.
keeper.thanks: The light turns again. Thank you, all of you.
keeper.optSerpent: Tell us about the Tide Serpent.
keeper.serpent1: Its seals are questions about angles: a leaning mast, a turn of the beam, and the circle’s own rule.
keeper.serpent2: Answer one and the seal breaks. Each new seal is a little harder.
keeper.survey1: The harbour wants to know how tall my lighthouse is. Nobody can climb it with a tape measure in this wind.
keeper.survey2: But you don’t need to climb. Stand back, measure the angle up to the top, and let tan do the climbing.
keeper.surveyText: You stand {dist} m from the lighthouse (the {2|distance}, the adjacent side) and look up to its top at {angle}°. Its {1|height} is the opposite side: height = distance × tan θ.
keeper.gHeight: The lighthouse: the side opposite the angle.
keeper.gDist: How far you stand from it: the side next to the angle.
keeper.surveyCap: The Lens is set to the angle you measured. The blue line on the wall is tan θ.
keeper.surveyHint: Read tan θ from the Lens (the tan wall), then multiply by the distance.
keeper.surveyStory: Measuring without climbing: an angle and a distance are enough.
keeper.surveyRetry: Hmm, that doesn’t match the old harbour records. Try again later.
keeper.surveyDone: Fourteen metres! Exactly what the old records say. And you never left the ground.
keeper.surveyMeri: That’s how navigators measure cliffs and distances at sea: one angle and one side.

aava.busy: Speak with the keeper first, sailors.

ren.busy: Kai! Talk to the keeper first, he knows what is going on.

gate.lockedAreas: A great iron gate with a dark lamp on top. Three ships are painted on it. It won’t open. (Clear the Tidepools, the Gull Cliffs and the Shipwreck Reef first.)
gate.lockedSkill: The painted ships seem to move, but you can’t read their angles yet. (Learn Tide Strike or Unbind first.)
gate.intro1: The gate’s lamp flickers. A voice rolls like surf: "Guide my three ships home, and I will open."
gate.intro2: Turn the beam onto each ship. 0° points east, 90° north, 180° west.
gate.story: Guide the ship home with the beam.
gate.ship1: Ship 1 is 8 km east and 8 km north. The beam must climb as much as it goes across: tan θ = 1. Turn the beam onto it.
gate.ship2: Ship 2 is straight north of the lighthouse. Straight up, the tip is not left or right at all: cos θ = 0. Turn the beam onto it.
gate.ship3: Ship 3 is 6 km west and 6 km north. Up as much as across, but to the west: tan θ = −1, between 90° and 180°. Turn the beam onto it.
gate.opened: The third ship turns for harbour. The lamp on the gate blazes, and the Beacon Gate swings open.
gate.meri: 45°, 90°, 135°: a quarter, a half and three quarters of a half turn. Just like a compass!

battle.pools1: Tide Crabs! They pinch harder at high tide, and the tide follows a sine wave.
battle.poolsTip1: Three heroes now: Kai, Aino and Meri. Meri throws her harpoon from range.
battle.poolsTip2: Tide Crabs hit ×1.5 at high tide and ×0.5 at low tide. Round 1 is high tide, then mid, low, mid: the tide is sin(round × 90°). The round counter shows it.
battle.poolsTip3: Strike hard at low tide, and keep your distance at high tide.
battle.cliffs1: Gulls diving from the cliffs, and those spiny urchins bite back!
battle.cliffsTip1: Storm Gulls peck from range and fly off after each attack.
battle.cliffsTip2: Sea Urchins have 2 armor and hurt whoever hits them with a learned attack. Focus pierces armor and is not reflected. Use the high cliffs for +damage.
battle.reef1: Drowned sailors, an eel and a siren. Careful, her song pulls you in!
battle.reefTip1: Drowned Sailors have 2 armor and follow the tide. The Spark Eel chills whoever it shocks (2 less AP next turn).
battle.reefTip2: The Siren pulls heroes in with her song and heals her allies. Take her down early.
battle.serpent1: WHO DARES TO TURN THE LIGHT?
battle.serpent2: MY COILS ARE ANGLES. MY TIDES ARE WAVES. DO YOU KNOW THEM?
battle.serpentMeri: Its seals are questions about angles! Answer them and they break.
battle.sealRule: While sealed, the Tide Serpent takes no damage. Break a seal to make it vulnerable (and lose a turn). At 70 and 35 HP a new seal forms. It has 2 armor and follows the tide: strongest at high tide.
battle.tipProbe: Kai, Tide Strike: one fast question, no working. 1/2, 0.5, √3/2 all work.
battle.tipUnbind: Aino, Unbind: work step by step with the Lens beside you.

win.pools: The crabs scuttle into the rock pools. The water settles; a path opens to the cliffs.
win.cliffs: The gulls wheel away over the sea. In a nest you find a Focus Tea.
win.reef: The sailors sink back into the reef and the siren falls silent. With all three places quiet, the lamp on the Beacon Gate starts to flicker.
win.serpent: The last seal breaks. The Tide Serpent uncoils and slides into the deep, and the tides roll in again: smooth, regular, a perfect sine wave.

ending.title: The light turns again!
ending.p1: Keeper Vilho lights the lamp. The beam sweeps the sea, its tip tracing a circle, its shadow on the water rising and falling like the tide.
ending.p2: You learned that sin and cos are the height and the width of a turning beam, that tan is where it hits the wall, and that waves are circles unrolled.
ending.p3: Next step for the curious: the sine and cosine rules for any triangle, and the waves of sound and light.
